questions.q: Why does the lab rule out String for the Risk Level field?
options: The requirement demands a fixed set of options, and free text would let someone type inconsistent values like "kinda high"
String fields can't be added to custom tables
String fields are always mandatory by default
String fields cannot be displayed on a form
questions.explain: A fixed set of options is exactly what Choice enforces at the platform level — String has no such constraint.

questions.q: In Step 2, why does the lab choose increasing numeric values (1, 2, 3, 4) for Low through Critical instead of leaving the value as text?
options: Numeric values are required by sys_choice and text values are not allowed
Numeric values make the field mandatory automatically
There is no reason; either choice behaves identically everywhere
Numeric values sort correctly by severity, where text values like "High" would sort alphabetically, out of order
questions.explain: A numeric value lets a future report filter or sort "High and above" correctly; a text value sorts alphabetically, not by severity.

questions.q: What does the sequence attribute on a sys_choice row control?
options: The stored value saved to the database
Whether the choice is active or inactive
The order options appear in the dropdown, independent of the stored value
Which table the choice list belongs to
questions.explain: Sequence controls display order only — you could renumber stored values later without disturbing the order users see.

questions.q: Why does the lab check the Mandatory flag on the risk_level dictionary entry?
options: Because all Choice fields are mandatory by default
Because the requirement explicitly says every assessment record needs a Risk Level set before it can be saved
Because Mandatory is required before a choice list can be attached to a field
Because the field would otherwise not appear on the form at all
questions.explain: Mandatory is the dictionary attribute that enforces exactly the save-time rule the requirement states — it's a deliberate decision tied to that specific requirement, not a default.

questions.q: What three decisions does this lab say are behind every field you'll ever add to any ServiceNow table?
options: Label, color, and position on the form
Table, column name, and sys_id
Active, Read-only, and Unique, in that order
Type, values (if a choice list applies), and constraints like Mandatory
questions.explain: Type, values, and constraints is the same three-decision sequence this lab walked through for Risk Level, and it generalizes to any field you build.
